The Oriental SaloonTombstoneDoc's at the card table. Pass the beans.Every recipe serves 4.
    Lunch CounterFrom the KitchenSweetsAt the Bar
    Lunch CounterOriental Saloon pickled eggsHard boiled eggs pickled for 3 days in a beet and vinegar brineHow to make it8 eggs250ml white vinegar125ml beetroot juice from a tin2 tbsp caster sugar1 tsp mustard seeds1 tsp black peppercornsBoil the eggs hard, cool and peel.Heat the vinegar, beetroot juice, sugar, mustard seeds and peppercorns.Pour over the eggs in a jar and leave in the fridge to pickle until pink.Drain and halve to serve.Faro night cornbreadCast iron cornbread, paid for by the Earps' stake in the saloon.How to make it150g fine cornmeal100g plain flour2 tsp baking powder250ml buttermilk1 egg140g butter2 tbsp honeyHeat a buttered cast iron pan in a 220°C oven.Mix the cornmeal, flour, baking powder, buttermilk, egg and melted butter briefly.Pour into the hot pan and bake.Beat softened butter with the honey and serve alongside.From the KitchenEarp brothers' chilliBeef braised with dried chillies. Skin that smokewagon and see what happens.How to make it1.2kg beef chuck1 brown onion4 garlic cloves4 dried chillies2 tsp ground cumin1 tin crushed tomatoesSoak the dried chillies in hot water, then blitz. Dice the beef, onion and garlic.Brown the beef in batches.Soften the onion and garlic, add the chillies, cumin and tomatoes.Braise covered until tender. Serve with the cornbread.Big Nose Kate's chicken and dumplingsThighs in thick broth, herbed buttermilk dough steamed on top, for Doc on a bad nightHow to make it800g chicken thigh fillets, in chunks30g butter1 onion, diced2 carrots, sliced2 celery sticks, sliced2 tbsp plain flour1 L chicken stock4 sprigs of thyme200g self-raising flour180ml buttermilk1 small bunch parsleyBrown the chicken in the butter, add the onion, carrot and celery and soften.Stir in the plain flour, then the stock and thyme, and simmer until the chicken is tender.Stir the self-raising flour, buttermilk, chopped parsley and a pinch of salt into a soft dough.Drop spoonfuls onto the simmering stew, cover tightly and cook without lifting the lid until the dumplings are puffed and cooked through.SweetsJosephine's peach pieLattice peach pie for Josephine and the travelling theatre troupe.How to make it6 peaches100g caster sugar1 lemon2 tbsp cornflour4 sheets of sweet shortcrust pastry300ml thickened creamSlice the peaches and toss with the sugar, lemon juice and cornflour.Line a pie dish with two pastry sheets, fill, and weave a lattice from the other two.Bake at 190°C.Cool slightly and serve with cream.At the BarDoc Holliday's rye old fashionedRye, demerara and orange bitters over one big ice cube. Say when.How to make it240ml rye whiskey2 tbsp demerara sugar8 dashes of orange bitters1 orangelarge ice cubes, to serveDissolve the demerara sugar in hot water and cool.Stir the whiskey, syrup and bitters with ice, one drink at a time.Strain over one large ice cube in a tumbler.Squeeze a strip of orange peel over the glass near a lit match so the oil flares, then drop it in.
